row.sso_plan: SSO license (Directories and identity management integration license)
row.evidence: Kisi's pricing page lists SSO and SCIM under a separate "Directories and identity management integration license", and the docs require "a valid, activated SSO license" before SSO or SCIM can be set up.
row.notes: Physical access control. Pricing is per organization (OSP Base from $99, Standard $199, Pro $299, Enterprise contact us; the page says discounts come with annual contracts and does not say whether the shown prices are monthly or annual), so per-user fields are null. SSO and SCIM are not in the OSP license itself: they sit under a separately licensed 'Directories and identity management integration license' whose price is not published, so status is gated with the add-on price as Contact Sales. Kisi's own integration pages disagree on the prerequisite (Entra page: 'Active Enterprise Kisi License'; Okta page: 'Kisi Organizations plan'); see conflicts. SCIM 2.0 at https://api.kisi.io/scim/v2 with a token generated by the org owner; SSO must be set up first; only one SSO/SCIM provider per organization. Kisi-built SCIM apps for Okta, Entra and JumpCloud; OneLogin uses its generic SCIM Provisioner. With Okta, users removed in Okta are only suspended in Kisi. Google Workspace, JumpCloud and Entra directory user imports are a separate non-SCIM sync.

auth.token_source: Kisi Settings > SSO & SCIM > Enable SCIM > Generate Token (organization owner; token shown once)
auth.notes: Microsoft's tutorial says long-lived bearer tokens are supported; Kisi does not state an expiry.

operations.notes: Docs do not say whether updates use PUT or PATCH; update support is from 'Update User Attributes' in the Okta guide.

deprovision.data_retained: Suspended users keep their account and can still sign in and see places, groups and other resources, but cannot open any locks. With OneLogin the admin can choose Delete instead, which removes the user from Kisi. Users removed in Okta are not removed in Kisi.

core: sendEmails (custom attribute in the core User namespace, set on create only)

custom.how: Map any IdP attribute to metadata.<name>; it is stored in the user's metadata object. sendEmails can be set only when the user is created.

attributes.notes: Microsoft's Entra tutorial lists userName, active, displayName, name.givenName, name.familyName, name.formatted for users and displayName, members, externalId for groups.

limitations.text: Only one SSO/SCIM provider per Kisi organization.
With Okta, users removed in Okta are not removed in Kisi; Kisi recommends regular audits and clean-up of suspended users.
Entra sync runs every 20-40 minutes after the initial sync.
The sendEmails attribute can only be set when a user is created and cannot be updated later.

auth.notes: Authorization: KISI-LOGIN <API_KEY>. Keys are created by organization admins or owners and expire after 6 months of inactivity unless created with expire: false.

endpoints.purpose: Fetch role assignments (access rights) for a user
Create role assignment (grant access right at group, place or organization level)

okta.notes: OIN page marks SAML, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking.

google.notes: SSO is a custom SAML app in Google Admin; provisioning is Kisi's Google Workspace Directory user import (non-SCIM).

onelogin.notes: Kisi's guide uses OneLogin's generic 'SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Core)' app, not a Kisi catalogue app.

jumpcloud.notes: Kisi docs: the Kisi SSO app in JumpCloud has an Identity Management tab for SCIM.

fallbacks.other_sync: Google Workspace Directory user import (also JumpCloud and Microsoft Entra ID directory imports listed on the pricing page)

citations.title: Identity management (SSO & SCIM)

conflicts.text: The pricing page puts SSO and SCIM under a separate 'Directories and identity management integration license' and the docs ask for 'a valid, activated SSO license', while Kisi's Entra integration page requires an 'Active Enterprise Kisi License' and its Okta page a 'Kisi Organizations plan'.

open_questions: The price of the directories and identity management (SSO) license is not published, and Kisi pages disagree on whether it needs an Enterprise license.
Docs do not say whether SCIM updates use PUT or PATCH, or whether filtering and pagination are supported (Entra's tutorial marks userName as filterable).
Whether suspending or deleting a user frees a paid seat is not documented (OSP plans are priced per organization with user caps).
Which plans include API access is not documented.
Whether Kisi is listed in the Google Workspace Marketplace or OneLogin catalogue was not checked (OneLogin blocks bots).
